caveats: All measurements are under the scheme reported in scheme_in_force.  A different scheme moves default sizes, colours, gridlines and the default legend position.

Tick VALUES are recovered by parsing the rendered tick LABEL back to a number.  Where a label is not numeric (explicit value "label" pairs) the value is null and only the exact pixel position is reported.
Pixel measurements are SVG user units on a 7.5in x 4.5in graph (viewBox 0 0 5400 3240); 14.4 units = 1 point.
xscale(noextend) shortens the drawn axis LINE to the outermost tick; it does not move the plotregion.  Compare axis_line_px with plotregion_px on those probes.
_meta.legend_oracle: Legend presence is a DIFFERENCE, never an inspection: every legend case is run twice, bare and with the legend off, and the anchorless <text> elements that disappear are the legend.  A second classifier (anchorless texts minus every mtextq() textbox string in the .gph) is recorded alongside, and is the one used where switching the legend off changed nothing.
_meta.method: Two oracles.  (1) The live-format .gph -- a plain-text graph-object script -- is authoritative for STRUCTURE: ring numbers, which side of the plotregion a textbox sits, and the verbatim editstyle directives an option produced.  It is NOT an oracle for tick positions: xlabel(#10) is stored as '.xaxis1.major.suggest_ticks 10' and the positions are computed at render time and never written to the file, drawn or not.  (2) Stata's own SVG writer gives the RENDERED result: the plotregion is the first solid-fill <rect> inside the graph region, tick marks are short black <line>s at a plotregion edge, tick labels are the row/column of <text> nearest that edge, gridlines are dashed multi-segment <line> groups, and legend keys are <text> elements with no text-anchor attribute.  Inverting the tick-pixel -> tick-value fit at the plotregion edges yields the axis range Stata actually used.
_meta.oracle_selfcheck: the same twoway command exported twice, more than a second apart, yields an identical text inventory: PASS

axis_range_extension.method: axis_low / axis_high are the DATA values at the two plotregion edges, obtained by inverting the tick-pixel -> tick-value map.  inner_low / inner_high are min/max over (data min/max, tick min/max): Stata first widens the axis to include every tick it decided to draw, then adds the margin.  The extension is the difference between the two.
axis_range_extension.pixel_margin_note: low_margin_px / high_margin_px are the gap, in SVG user units, between a plotregion edge and the extreme value the axis had to contain.  Probes b_size_wide / b_size_tall / b_size_square vary xsize()/ysize() so that a margin fixed in absolute units can be told apart from one that is a fixed fraction of the plotregion.  Across all four graph shapes probed the margin is the same on all four sides and is a constant fraction of min(canvas width, canvas height) -- see margin_over_min_canvas_dimension_values.

legend_rule.oracle: Every case was run twice -- bare and with the legend switched off -- exported to SVG, and the anchorless <text> elements that disappear were counted as legend keys.  Where switching the legend off changed nothing (it does not under by(..., legend(off)) for the enclosing graph), a second classifier was used instead: anchorless texts minus every mtextq() textbox string recorded in the .gph.  Both verdicts are stored per case and any disagreement is listed.
